events.title: Priestley Isolates Oxygen
events.description: English chemist and clergyman Joseph Priestley focused sunlight on mercuric oxide and released a colorless gas. He called it "dephlogisticated air". The gas was later named oxygen.
events.significance: The experiment is one of the landmark moments in the history of chemistry. It changed how scientists understood air, combustion and respiration.

events.title: Slavery Abolition Act Takes Effect
events.description: The British Slavery Abolition Act received Royal Assent in 1833. It came into force on this day across most of the British Empire, ending legal slavery in those territories. The Act also set up a compensation scheme for slave owners.
events.significance: The Act was a major turning point in the global movement against slavery. Emancipation Day is still marked on August 1 in many former British colonies.

events.title: The Warsaw Uprising Begins
events.description: The Polish Home Army rose against the German occupiers of Warsaw, hoping to liberate the city as Soviet forces drew near. The fighting lasted about two months.
events.significance: It was the largest single resistance operation of the Second World War in occupied Europe. It remains a powerful symbol of Polish courage and sacrifice.

events.title: MTV Goes on the Air
events.description: At 12:01 AM, MTV: Music Television launched on cable with a countdown and the words "Ladies and gentlemen, rock and roll." The first video it played was "Video Killed the Radio Star" by The Buggles.
events.significance: MTV reshaped the music industry and youth culture. It made the music video a central part of how pop music was marketed and enjoyed.
